chapters.1.meaning: Solomon asks for wisdom to lead the people. God grants wisdom and also gives him wealth.
chapters.1.lds: Why does Solomon ask for wisdom before asking for wealth?
chapters.2.lds: Whose skills and labor make the temple possible?
chapters.3.meaning: The temple’s rooms and decorations set apart a place for worship. Gold and carved figures mark its inner spaces.
chapters.4.lds: What different tasks do the temple’s vessels serve?
chapters.5.meaning: The ark recalls God’s covenant with Israel. Music and a cloud mark its arrival in the temple.
chapters.6.lds: Why does Solomon include foreigners in his prayer?
chapters.7.meaning: God calls the people to humble themselves, pray, and turn from wrong. The promise also warns against abandoning him.
chapters.8.lds: How do workers and sailors support Solomon’s kingdom?
chapters.9.summary: The queen of Sheba tests Solomon with questions. Gifts and trade bring him wealth. Rehoboam becomes king after his death.
chapters.9.lds: What does the queen ask about Solomon’s wisdom and God’s care for Israel?
chapters.10.lds: Why does Rehoboam reject the advice to ease the people’s burden?
chapters.11.summary: Shemaiah stops Rehoboam’s attack on the northern tribes. Rehoboam strengthens towns and welcomes priests and Levites. He also plans which son will rule.
chapters.11.lds: Why do priests and Levites leave the northern kingdom?
chapters.12.lds: How does Rehoboam respond when Shemaiah explains Judah’s defeat?
chapters.13.summary: Abijah appeals to David’s covenant and temple worship while confronting Jeroboam. Judah wins the battle.
chapters.13.meaning: Abijah argues that Judah still keeps God’s temple service. In battle, Judah’s people call on God.
chapters.13.lds: What reasons does Abijah give for Judah’s trust in God?
chapters.14.meaning: Asa prays when a larger army approaches. He asks God to help those with little strength.
chapters.15.meaning: Asa renews the covenant and removes his grandmother’s royal standing. The agreement also threatens death for refusing to seek God.
chapters.17.lds: How does Jehoshaphat use teachers to help his people learn God’s law?
chapters.21.meaning: Jehoram kills his brothers to secure his throne. Revolts, invasion, and illness follow his harmful rule.
chapters.21.lds: How do Jehoram’s choices affect his brothers and the people he rules?
chapters.22.meaning: Athaliah attacks the royal children. Jehoshabeath saves Joash, keeping a future king alive.
chapters.22.lds: What do Jehoshabeath and the nurse risk by hiding Joash?
chapters.23.meaning: Jehoiada gathers support for the hidden king. Crowning Joash ends Athaliah’s rule and leads to renewed worship.
chapters.23.lds: Why does Jehoiada join the king’s crowning with a covenant?
chapters.24.lds: Why does Joash reject correction after Jehoiada’s death?
chapters.25.lds: How does Amaziah respond differently to his two warnings?
chapters.26.meaning: Uzziah’s success leads to pride. The priests challenge his attempt to take over their temple duty.
chapters.27.summary: Jotham strengthens Jerusalem and other towns. Ammon pays him tribute. He follows God, but the people continue doing wrong.
chapters.27.meaning: Jotham follows his father’s good example without entering the temple. His people still make different choices.
chapters.27.lds: What can a faithful leader do when others continue doing wrong?
chapters.28.lds: How do the northern leaders turn a victory into care for their captives?
chapters.29.lds: What work must the priests and Levites finish before temple worship can begin again?
chapters.30.meaning: Hezekiah welcomes people who have not kept every preparation rule. He prays for their pardon and healing.
chapters.31.lds: How do careful storage and fair sharing support the temple workers’ families?
chapters.32.meaning: Hezekiah prepares defenses and encourages the people. He and Isaiah pray as Assyria threatens Jerusalem.
chapters.35.meaning: Neco warns Josiah against joining the battle. Josiah refuses the warning and dies from his wounds.
chapters.35.lds: Why does Josiah’s earlier faithfulness not settle what he should do in this battle?
people.heman-singer.meaning: Later singers serve in Heman’s family line. His name keeps their earlier musical service in memory.
people.jeduthun.meaning: Jeduthun’s descendants continue singing at later temple celebrations.
people.queen-sheba.meaning: She tests Solomon with questions and speaks her judgment of his wisdom.
people.jesse.meaning: Jeroboam calls David the son of Jesse when rejecting Rehoboam’s rule.
people.mahalath-rehoboam.meaning: The chapter names three sons born to Mahalath and Rehoboam.
people.abihail-rehoboam.role: Woman named in Rehoboam’s family record
people.zerah-cushite.meaning: Zerah brings a large army to Mareshah. Asa calls on God before the battle.
people.hanani-seer.relations: He warns Asa about his alliance and is imprisoned. Jehu is later named as Hanani’s son.
people.ahab-prophets.meaning: These prophets promise victory. Micaiah challenges the message they share with Ahab.
people.amariah-chief.meaning: Amariah oversees matters concerning God’s law. Zebadiah oversees the king’s matters.
people.elijah.meaning: Elijah’s letter condemns Jehoram’s killings and worship. It warns of harm to his household and people.
people.omri.meaning: Ahaziah’s family ties connect him with Omri’s royal house in the north.
people.jehu-nimshi.meaning: Jehu kills Joram and Ahaziah during his attack on Ahab’s royal family.
people.jehosheba.meaning: She hides Joash and his nurse. Her marriage to Jehoiada connects the rescue with the temple.
people.zibiah.meaning: Zibiah is Joash’s mother. The book identifies Beersheba as her hometown.
people.jehozabad.meaning: Jehozabad helps kill Joash after the king’s attack on Zechariah.
people.amaziah-prophet.meaning: He asks why Amaziah trusts gods that failed to save their own people.
people.obed-edom-amaziah.meaning: Temple treasures under Obed-Edom’s care are taken after Amaziah’s defeat.
people.azariah.meaning: Uzziah builds towns and strengthens farming and defense. His pride later brings conflict with the priests.
people.zechariah-uzziah.meaning: Zechariah helps Uzziah seek God during the king’s early years.
people.jotham.meaning: Jotham prepares his ways before God. The book distinguishes his choices from his people’s wrongdoing.
people.jerushah.meaning: Jotham’s opening record names Jerushah as his mother and Zadok as her father.
people.pul.role: Assyrian ruler whom Ahaz asks for help
people.pul.meaning: Ahaz gives him temple and palace treasures. The alliance brings pressure instead of relief.
people.captive-care-leaders.relations: Azariah is Johanan’s son. Berechiah is Meshillemoth’s son. Jehizkiah is Shallum’s son. Amasa is Hadlai’s son.
people.conaniah-hezekiah.meaning: Conaniah oversees temple supplies. His brother Shimei helps him keep and share the offerings.
people.amon-king.meaning: Amon continues his father’s earlier wrongdoing but refuses to humble himself. His servants kill him.
people.necho.role: Egyptian king who warns Josiah and later controls Judah
people.necho.meaning: Neco warns Josiah to stay out of his war. He later removes Jehoahaz and demands payment.
people.jeremiah.meaning: Jeremiah laments Josiah’s death. The closing chapter also connects him with warnings about exile.
people.samuel.meaning: Josiah’s Passover is compared with celebrations since Samuel’s days.
people.jehoiakim.meaning: Babylon attacks Jehoiakim and takes temple vessels. The notice leads into Judah’s final losses.
people.jehoiachin.meaning: Chronicles gives his age as eight when he becomes king. Second Kings 24:8 gives eighteen.
places.gibeon.summary: The meeting tent and bronze altar are at Gibeon. Solomon seeks God there.
places.jerusalem.summary: Judah’s kings rule from Jerusalem. Its temple becomes the center of the book’s worship accounts.
places.tyre.summary: Huram rules Tyre and sends timber, skilled work, and sailors to help Solomon.
places.jordan.summary: Solomon’s bronze vessels are cast in the Jordan plain between Succoth and Zeredah.
places.hamath.summary: Hamath marks the northern reach of the gathering for Solomon’s temple dedication.
places.edom.summary: Edom rebels against Jehoram. Amaziah later defeats its forces and takes its gods.
places.hebron.summary: Rehoboam strengthens Hebron among Judah’s defended towns.
places.mareshah.summary: Asa meets Zerah’s army near Mareshah. Eliezer, who warns Jehoshaphat, also comes from this town.
places.dan.summary: Asa’s Syrian ally attacks Dan among the northern towns.
places.jericho.summary: Northern leaders bring Judah’s injured captives to their relatives at Jericho.
